data.name: Palvinder
data.gender_notes: Palvinder is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who protects and rules over the fort or the kingdom. Derived from the Sanskrit words Pala (protector) and Vindra (fort, kingdom). The name Palvinder carries the meaning “Lord of the Fort” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Punjabi. Parents who choose Palvinder usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of the fort and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for a protector, a leader, and a warrior of the divine realm. Signifies courage, strength, and the power to overcome challenges
data.etymology: Palvinder belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of the Fort.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Palvinder total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Palvinder signifies power, authority, and protection. This name was common among the warriors and rulers in Hindu culture. The name honors individuals who have shown strength, courage, and leadership, inspiring reverence and respect within their communities.
data.spiritual_significance: At the heart of the name Palvinder is the concept of protection. In Hindu philosophy, the ultimate protector is the divine paladin, Shiva, who guards against evil and destruction. Palvinder carries the responsibility of embodying this nobility of character, striving to protect those around them and upholding the universal ethical principles. The spiritual significance of the name calls us to cultivate inner fortitude, wisdom, and compassion, permitting us to fulfill our roles as protectors of our families, communities, and personal values.

historical_references.reference: Palvinder was the name of a powerful Jat ruler in the 17th century who ruled over the area that is now Haryana, India. He was a prominent figure in the Jat rebellion against the Mughals.
historical_references.context: The Jat rebellion against the Mughals was a series of uprisings by the Jats, a farming community in northern India, against the Mughal Empire. Palvinder was a key leader in this rebellion, which lasted from 1669 to 1675.

historical_references.reference: Palvinder is also the name of a village in the Punjab region of India, which has been mentioned in historical records dating back to the 16th century. It was a significant center of Sikh religious and cultural activity.
historical_references.context: During this period, Punjab was a center of Sikh religious and cultural activity. Palvinder village was an important settlement for Sikh communities, and it played a significant role in the development of Sikhism as a major world religion.
